name: pdf-inspector
description: Fast Rust library for PDF inspection, classification, and text extraction. Intelligently detects scanned vs text-based PDFs to enable smart routing decisions.
one_liner: A fast behind-the-scenes tool that looks at a PDF and instantly tells you whether it's a real digital document or just a scanned image — so you don't waste money running expensive OCR on documents that don't need it.
buyer: An engineer building a document-processing or AI chatbot product who needs to cut their OCR bill by not OCR-ing PDFs that are already text.
business_use_cases: A legal-tech startup routes scanned contracts to expensive OCR while sending text-native PDFs straight to fast extraction, cutting processing costs significantly.
A fintech company building loan-document ingestion uses it to pre-classify thousands of incoming PDFs before deciding how much OCR budget to spend.
An AI 'chat with your documents' product uses it as the first step in its ingestion pipeline to keep costs down at scale.

money_ideas.idea: Wrap it in a hosted API and charge per document processed for teams who don't want to run Rust infrastructure themselves.
Offer integration consulting for enterprises building document pipelines who want it wired into their existing stack.

steal_this: Stand up a simple hosted API this weekend — 'upload a PDF, get back scanned-or-not plus clean markdown' — and charge per call; it's pure infrastructure with obvious enterprise demand.
